title: `requirements.txt` is invalid
body:
`requirements.txt` contains embedded UTF-16-style null bytes in the Flask requirement. A clean `pip install -r requirements.txt` fails.

**Fix:** replace the corrupted line with a normal UTF-8 requirement such as `flask>=3.0.0`, and preferably pin tested dependency versions.

title: `resume.get_variant()` does not exist
body:
`composer.py` calls `resume.get_variant(...)`, but `resume.py` has no such function. Compose/follow-up flows that specify a resume variant can fail with `AttributeError`.

**Fix:** add a proper lookup function or use a repository `get_by_id()` method consistently.

title: Editing a draft automatically approves it
body:
`repository.py` updates content and also changes status to `approved`. This breaks the stated human-review guarantee.

**Expected:** `Save Edits -> pending_review`, `Approve -> approved`.

title: Web send endpoint bypasses the send window
body:
`run_send_batch()` defaults to `force=True`, and the web endpoint calls it without overriding that value. The web UI can therefore send outside the configured send window.

**Fix:** default to `force=False`; require an explicit, deliberate override.

title: Daily/company send limits can be bypassed by changing status
body:
Quota queries count only rows whose current status is `sent`. Once a message becomes `replied`, `ghosted`, `bounced`, `offer`, etc., it stops counting toward the quota.

**Fix:** base quotas on historical send evidence such as `sent_at IS NOT NULL`, not the current status.

title: SMTP success followed by DB failure can duplicate an email
body:
If SMTP accepts a message but the subsequent DB update fails, retrying can send the same email again.

**Fix:** introduce explicit send states, idempotency keys, and durable send-attempt records.

title: Concurrent send requests can send the same email twice
body:
Two requests can both read the same approved queue before either updates the row. UI button disabling is not concurrency control.

**Fix:** atomically claim messages using a `sending` state or DB locking/claim pattern.

title: `sendmail()` refusal results are ignored
body:
`server.sendmail()` can return a dictionary of refused recipients. The code treats the call as successful without checking that result.

**Fix:** inspect the return value and do not mark a refused message as sent.

title: Research evidence is generated but discarded
body:
AI research notes are produced but not persisted in the database or surfaced to the reviewer. The system loses the evidence behind personalization.

**Fix:** store research facts, source URLs/titles, timestamps, and grounding metadata.

title: No authentication/authorization
body:
The application exposes contact data, drafts, approval, reply checks, and send actions without an authentication layer.

**Fix:** add authentication, authorization, CSRF protection, and safe deployment defaults before remote/private-cloud exposure.

---

title: Fresh installation may not initialize the DB with Flask CLI
body:
DB initialization is inside `if __name__ == "__main__"`, while the README instructs using `flask run`. Under Flask CLI, that initialization block does not execute.

**Fix:** initialize schema explicitly through startup/app factory or a CLI command.

title: Test suite is broken and not isolated
body:
The current test setup performs live HTTP requests, lacks proper assertions, and fails during collection if the server is not running.

**Fix:** use Flask's test client, mocks, fixtures, and temporary databases.

title: `test_context.py` modifies production data/files while being collected
body:
The test writes to `context.txt` immediately on import and therefore changes application state merely by running tests.

**Fix:** delete/rewrite it as a genuine test using a temporary fixture.

title: Running tests can contaminate the AI candidate context
body:
The test writes a Rust/OS persona into `context.txt`; this file is then used as candidate context for AI generation.

**Fix:** never mutate production context from tests; isolate all test state.

title: Bundled virtual environment is Windows-specific
body:
The archive contains a Windows virtualenv whose interpreter paths are tied to the original machine.

**Fix:** distribute source plus dependency/lock files, not `venv/`.

title: `venv/` is unnecessarily included in the archive
body:
The ZIP contains a ~73 MB environment artifact rather than a clean source distribution.

**Fix:** ignore virtualenvs in source control/releases.

title: `__pycache__`/`.pyc` artifacts are included
body:
Python bytecode should not be included in the source release.

**Fix:** remove them and add ignore rules.

title: `.git/` is included in the ZIP
body:
The archive contains repository history, configuration, reflogs, and metadata.

**Fix:** exclude `.git/` from release archives.

title: Git history retains old project data
body:
Deleted/changed files can remain recoverable from `.git`, including historical `context.txt` content.

**Fix:** keep Git history out of releases; if sensitive data was ever committed publicly, rotate/remove it properly.

title: Release archive includes persistent DB artifacts
body:
The ZIP contains SQLite databases with application/test data.

**Fix:** generate databases on first run or ship sanitized seed data separately.

title: Release archive includes the resume PDF
body:
A personal resume should not be bundled in a distributable/public archive unless intentionally public.

**Fix:** exclude it and make resume paths user-configurable.

title: Release archive includes personal/test contact data
body:
The database contains contacts, suppression records, and outreach history.

**Fix:** release source separately from private runtime data.

title: No actual credential was found in the repository scan, but packaging still exposes too much
body:
No obvious API key/private key pattern was found, but `.git`, DBs, resume, and personal data are still inappropriate in a public release.

**Fix:** implement a clean release pipeline and secret scan.

title: Dependency versions are too loosely specified
body:
Core dependencies use broad minimum versions, especially the rapidly changing Google GenAI SDK.

**Fix:** pin known-good versions or use a lock file and test upgrade cadence.

title: Configured Gemini model is hardcoded in code
body:
The application appears to expose model configuration, but the actual model string is hardcoded.

**Fix:** load it from validated configuration.

title: `RESUME_DIR` configuration exists but is inconsistently used
body:
The code defines a resume directory abstraction but often handles resume paths directly.

**Fix:** centralize all filesystem resolution through `BASE_DIR`/`RESUME_DIR`.

title: Relative `context.txt` path depends on current working directory
body:
Using `open("context.txt")` means behavior changes depending on where the app is launched from.

**Fix:** resolve from `config.BASE_DIR`.

title: Relative static path depends on current working directory
body:
`send_from_directory('static', ...)` has the same working-directory fragility.

**Fix:** use Flask's configured static/template directories.

title: `debug=True` is unsafe outside development
body:
Running the application directly can expose Flask's interactive debugger.

**Fix:** make debug mode environment-controlled and default to false.

title: Application startup config validation is incomplete
body:
Invalid settings can be discovered only when a feature is used.

**Fix:** validate all required settings and ranges once at startup.

---

title: Missing `sent_at` semantics cause quota integrity problems
body:
Current quota logic relies on mutable status rather than immutable send evidence.

**Fix:** treat `sent_at` (or a send event) as historical fact.

title: Timezone handling is inconsistent between quota and send window
body:
Quota uses SQLite's UTC `date('now')`, while send-window logic uses local Python time.

**Fix:** standardize on UTC storage and explicit application timezone conversion.

title: Follow-up date comparisons have the same timezone mismatch
body:
`date.today()` and DB timestamps can represent different calendar dates around midnight.

**Fix:** define one timezone policy and apply it consistently.

title: Send window only supports whole hours
body:
You cannot express windows such as 09:30–17:45.

**Fix:** store/send by minutes or timezone-aware datetime intervals if needed.

title: `SEND_START_HOUR`/`SEND_END_HOUR` semantics are implicit
body:
The implementation effectively uses a half-open interval (`start <= hour < end`) but does not document it.

**Fix:** document boundary behavior.

title: `SEND_DAYS` accepts arbitrary invalid values
body:
Typos can silently disable sending or produce confusing behavior.

**Fix:** validate against known weekday values.

title: `MIN_DELAY_SECONDS > MAX_DELAY_SECONDS` is not validated
body:
This can make `random.randint()` fail at runtime.

**Fix:** validate min/max ordering at startup.

title: Negative delay configuration is allowed
body:
Negative values create nonsensical timing semantics.

**Fix:** require non-negative durations.

title: Negative daily/company caps are allowed
body:
Negative caps create nonsensical queue behavior.

**Fix:** require positive/non-negative values.

title: Suppressed messages can consume batch slots
body:
The queue is sliced to the quota before suppression filtering.

**Fix:** filter non-sendable messages before applying send-slot selection.

title: Suppressed messages can distort company quota selection
body:
Company counts can be incremented before suppression exclusion.

**Fix:** count only actually sendable candidates.

title: Suppression should be normalized case-insensitively
body:
`jane@acme.com` and `Jane@Acme.com` can be treated as different values.

**Fix:** canonicalize emails to lowercase and trimmed form before all comparisons.

title: `INSERT OR REPLACE` destroys suppression history timestamps
body:
SQLite `REPLACE` can delete and recreate the row, resetting the original timestamp.

**Fix:** use `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` without replacing the original creation time.

title: Suppression has no reason taxonomy
body:
Reasons are arbitrary strings.

**Fix:** standardize reasons such as unsubscribe, bounce, manual, invalid, recruiter request, etc.

title: Suppression has no audit/history model
body:
You cannot tell who/what added or removed a suppression and why it changed.

**Fix:** record suppression events or immutable history.

title: SMTP connection lacks explicit timeout
body:
Connection attempts can hang, especially inside a synchronous HTTP request.

**Fix:** specify explicit network timeouts.

title: SMTP session is not recreated after a mid-batch connection failure
body:
One dead SMTP session can cause all later messages to fail.

**Fix:** reconnect/re-authenticate when appropriate.

title: Retry logic treats all errors alike
body:
Permanent errors are retried unnecessarily, while transient errors need targeted retry policy.

**Fix:** classify retryable vs non-retryable errors.

title: Retry uses fixed delay instead of exponential backoff/jitter
body:
A fixed sleep is crude for provider throttling/transient outages.

**Fix:** use bounded exponential backoff with jitter.

title: AI retry block does not include the actual API call
body:
The Gemini request occurs outside the `try` block. Network/rate-limit errors therefore are not retried.

**Fix:** wrap the API invocation and parsing in a proper retry policy.

title: SMTP failures are recorded as human `rejected`
body:
Transport failure is conceptually different from a user rejecting a draft.

**Fix:** introduce states such as `send_failed`, `retry_pending`, or equivalent.

title: No durable send-attempt log
body:
There is no first-class record of attempts, timestamps, SMTP responses, retries, and failures.

**Fix:** create a `send_attempts` table.

title: No send idempotency key
body:
There is no durable identifier preventing duplicate delivery after retries or concurrency races.

**Fix:** create deterministic/unique send attempt IDs and claim semantics.

title: Sending is performed synchronously inside an HTTP request
body:
The request can remain open for many minutes because of deliberate random delays.

**Fix:** background worker/job queue.

title: Worst-case batch duration can approach an hour or more
body:
A 15-email batch with 45–240 second delays can take ~56 minutes before retries and connection time.

**Fix:** move sending outside request/response lifecycle.

title: No send job progress tracking
body:
The UI has no persistent concept of a running batch, current item, failures, or completion state.

**Fix:** create a `send_jobs`/job-progress model.

title: Send button has no confirmation step
body:
Sending is irreversible, yet the UI can trigger it directly.

**Fix:** show a pre-send confirmation with count, cap, window, and risk summary.

title: UI does not show quota before send
body:
The operator cannot see daily/company limits or how many slots remain.

**Fix:** expose quota state in the confirmation UI.

title: Batch result count is wrong in the UI
body:
`summary.length` is presented as the number sent even though summary entries can be skipped/failed/dry-run.

**Fix:** count records with actual success status.

title: SMTP is opened before all suppression filtering is complete
body:
The app may authenticate to Gmail even when there are no sendable messages.

**Fix:** fully prefilter the queue before opening SMTP.

---

title: No explicit email state machine
body:
Any arbitrary status can be written; transitions are not centrally validated.

**Fix:** define allowed transitions and enforce them in service/repository code and preferably DB constraints.

title: Unsupported status actions can return success
body:
An invalid status value such as `banana` can return success without changing anything.

**Fix:** reject unknown actions with a 4xx response.

title: Updating a nonexistent email can return success
body:
Update queries do not consistently inspect affected-row counts.

**Fix:** return 404 when the target row does not exist.

title: Status updates can mutate impossible states
body:
Nothing prevents transitions such as `approved -> replied` when never sent, or `replied -> approved`.

**Fix:** enforce state transition rules.

title: Historical status is lost
body:
The current status overwrites the previous lifecycle state.

**Fix:** add an immutable `status_events`/`outreach_events` table.

title: Email status and transport state are overloaded into one field
body:
Human review, sending, delivery, conversation, and hiring outcomes are all mixed together.

**Fix:** separate workflow state from delivery/conversation events.

title: `rejected` is overloaded
body:
A human rejecting a draft and a transport failure are represented using the same concept.

**Fix:** separate `rejected`, `send_failed`, `cancelled`, `suppressed`, etc.

title: Schema status documentation is stale
body:
Schema comments omit statuses that the UI actually uses, such as interview/offer outcomes.

**Fix:** centralize and document allowed state values.

title: `updated_at` is not reliably updated on content edit
body:
Content mutations can retain an old timestamp.

**Fix:** update `updated_at` on every mutation.

title: `update_sent()` does not reliably verify row existence
body:
A failed update can look like a successful operation.

**Fix:** check `rowcount`.

title: No recipient/company consistency constraint
body:
An email can be composed with a company ID unrelated to the contact's actual company.

**Fix:** validate the relationship server-side before composition.

title: Historical email does not snapshot recipient data
body:
If contact/company information changes later, historical emails can display current relational data rather than what was actually sent.

**Fix:** snapshot `to_email`, recipient name, company name, etc. on the email record.

title: `follow_up_to_email_id` needs stronger semantics
body:
It currently functions as an existence check rather than a workflow relation with explicit active/sent/rejected semantics.

**Fix:** treat follow-ups as first-class outreach records/events.

title: Follow-up queries block future follow-ups after any child exists
body:
A rejected historical follow-up still makes the original look already followed-up.

**Fix:** exclude only active/sent follow-ups, not every child row.

title: Follow-up endpoint does not enforce due date
body:
The backend can generate a follow-up even when the UI would normally not show the message as due.

**Fix:** enforce business rules on the server.

title: Follow-up is allowed for `replied`
body:
A contact who already replied is usually in a conversation, not a “no response” follow-up state.

**Fix:** define separate conversation handling or narrow eligible statuses.

title: `follow_up_due` is effectively dead schema
body:
The field exists but due dates are dynamically calculated instead.

**Fix:** either remove it or make it authoritative.

title: Company/contact relationship is not enforced at DB level
body:
Foreign keys alone do not ensure that a contact belongs to the company referenced by an email.

**Fix:** enforce relationship at service layer and structure data around consistent foreign keys.

title: No DB CHECK constraint for valid statuses
body:
SQLite can accept arbitrary status strings.

**Fix:** add a CHECK constraint or dedicated lookup table where appropriate.

title: No unique outbound message ID constraint/index
body:
`message_id` is important for reply matching and should be indexed/unique when present.

**Fix:** add a unique index/constraint and validate provider IDs.

---

title: Duplicate contacts already exist
body:
The database contains duplicate addresses for the same company/contact context.

**Fix:** normalize emails and enforce uniqueness.

title: `add_contact()` does not use duplicate-detection logic
body:
A lookup helper exists, but insertion does not consistently use it.

**Fix:** enforce dedupe centrally and in the DB.

title: Email uniqueness is not enforced by the DB
body:
Without a uniqueness constraint, race conditions can still create duplicate contacts.

**Fix:** unique index on `(company_id, normalized_email)` or equivalent model.

title: Email normalization is inconsistent
body:
Whitespace/casing are not consistently canonicalized on ingestion and comparison.

**Fix:** normalize once at the boundary.

title: Suppression lookup is vulnerable to case mismatch
body:
Case differences can bypass a suppression record.

**Fix:** canonical email storage.

title: Email ingestion only performs syntax validation
body:
A richer MX validator exists but is not consistently used by contact/CSV ingestion.

**Fix:** apply a clear validation policy at ingestion.

title: `has_mx_record()` conflates DNS failure with no mail server
body:
`NoNameservers` is handled as a definitive failure rather than “could not verify.”

**Fix:** distinguish `valid`, `invalid`, and `unknown` DNS outcomes.

title: No-MX does not necessarily mean undeliverable
body:
Mail delivery can fall back to A/AAAA in some cases; lack of MX is not identical to impossible delivery.

**Fix:** treat the validator as advisory and model uncertainty explicitly.

title: CSV company matching can merge unrelated companies with the same domain
body:
Domain-first matching can return the wrong company before checking name identity.

**Fix:** normalize and match using a deliberate hierarchy.

title: CSV importer can create multiple companies for equivalent names/domains
body:
Company normalization is too weak to guarantee canonical identity.

**Fix:** use canonical company/domain keys and DB uniqueness where appropriate.

title: CSV importer only supports one job posting per company naturally
body:
Job data lives directly on the company, so importing multiple roles for one company overwrites/complicates the model.

**Fix:** introduce `job_postings` as a first-class entity.

title: CSV template comment row is treated as data
body:
The example comment can produce an avoidable validation error.

**Fix:** remove it or support comment rows explicitly.

title: CSV importer creates duplicate contacts
body:
Repeated rows are inserted without robust canonical dedupe.

**Fix:** dedupe in service + DB.

title: CSV upload path can collide on identical filenames
body:
Using a predictable temp path based on the uploaded filename can create races.

**Fix:** use a unique temporary file path.

title: CSV upload has no size limit
body:
There is no obvious `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH` safeguard.

**Fix:** cap upload size.

title: CSV parser silently accepts unknown columns
body:
Unexpected fields are not clearly reported.

**Fix:** validate headers and report extras/missing columns.

title: CSV encoding support is narrow
body:
Only UTF-8 with BOM is assumed. Windows-generated CSVs can use other encodings.

**Fix:** detect/fallback gracefully or normalize input requirements.

title: Empty/malformed CSVs are not handled robustly
body:
Missing headers or empty files can lead to awkward downstream behavior.

**Fix:** explicitly validate `fieldnames` and row structure.

title: CSV import is not preview-first
body:
Uploading immediately mutates the production DB.

**Fix:** implement upload -> validate/preview -> confirm -> import.

title: CSV import is not clearly transactional
body:
Partial failure can leave partial imports without an explicit policy.

**Fix:** support all-or-nothing mode or clearly report partial results.

title: CSV error tuples are not a clean API structure
body:
Errors are accumulated as tuples that become arrays over JSON serialization.

**Fix:** return structured objects such as `{row, error}`.

title: Company add endpoint lacks strong validation
body:
Blank/invalid names, domains, and URLs can enter the database.

**Fix:** validate and normalize at the API boundary.

title: Company domain normalization is incomplete
body:
Equivalent representations (`https://`, `www.`, case, trailing dot, etc.) are not consistently canonicalized.

**Fix:** canonicalize domains before lookup/storage.

title: `normalize_company_name()` is too minimal for identity
body:
It handles whitespace/trailing periods but not broader legal suffix/punctuation variants.

**Fix:** improve normalization only if company dedupe requires it.

title: Dead `pass` logic in `find_company_by_name()`
body:
The function contains a no-op branch that indicates incomplete logic.

**Fix:** remove dead code and simplify matching flow.

title: Dead/inconsistent `find_contact_without_email()` logic
body:
The schema requires an email, conflicting with logic intended to find contacts without one.

**Fix:** remove the obsolete path or redesign the schema intentionally.

title: No contact/company edit UI
body:
The application can add data but has weak management tools for correcting it.

**Fix:** provide edit/merge/archive actions.

title: No contact/company delete/archive strategy
body:
There is no clear lifecycle for stale/incorrect records.

**Fix:** define soft-delete/archive semantics that preserve historical outreach.

title: No contact merge tool
body:
Duplicates can accumulate without an operational way to merge them safely.

**Fix:** add duplicate detection and merge workflow.

title: No data-cleanup workflow
body:
Test records and stale contacts can remain indefinitely.

**Fix:** build safe cleanup/archiving capabilities.

---

title: Automatic resume selection is disconnected from the web flow
body:
Current web composition does not send `resume_variant_id`, so the existing resume-selection logic is not actually used in the normal UI flow.

**Fix:** wire automatic selection into the compose service and persist the chosen variant.

title: Resume management is inaccessible from the web UI
body:
The backend has resume-variant functions, but users cannot conveniently add/manage/select variants in the UI.

**Fix:** add a Resume Management screen.

title: Resume variant lookup is inefficient
body:
Sender code appears to load all variants and scan them instead of fetching a single ID.

**Fix:** query by primary key.

title: `ResumeRepository.get_by_id()` is missing
body:
This omission helped cause the missing `resume.get_variant()` bug.

**Fix:** add a canonical repository method.

title: Resume keyword matching uses naive substring matching
body:
Short tokens can match unrelated substrings (`sql` in `nosql`, etc.).

**Fix:** token-aware matching or phrase/word-boundary scoring.

title: Resume keyword scores are too simplistic
body:
All matched keywords effectively have similar importance.

**Fix:** weight required skills, titles, exact phrases, and stronger role signals.

title: Resume ties are resolved arbitrarily
body:
Equal scores fall back to insertion order.

**Fix:** define deterministic secondary ranking or manual preference.

title: Relative resume paths depend on working directory
body:
`Path(resume_path).exists()` can fail depending on launch directory.

**Fix:** resolve against `BASE_DIR`/`RESUME_DIR`.

title: Missing resume files can silently result in no attachment
body:
A required resume can disappear from the outgoing message without stopping the send.

**Fix:** fail safely or require an explicit link-only policy.

title: `RESUME_ATTACH_MODE` accepts invalid values silently
body:
Unexpected configuration can produce ambiguous behavior.

**Fix:** validate enum-like config values.

title: Link mode can silently fall back to attachment mode
body:
`attach` becomes effectively the fallback if no URL is present.

**Fix:** fail configuration or make fallback behavior explicit.

title: Resume files are not validated as actual PDFs
body:
A `.pdf` path is not enough to guarantee the content is a valid PDF.

**Fix:** validate file type/signature when adding/updating resumes.

title: Resume lifecycle is incomplete
body:
No strong edit/replace/delete/deactivate semantics are exposed.

**Fix:** support full variant lifecycle management.

title: Profile setup is not exposed in the web workflow
body:
Profile data exists, but onboarding/configuration is largely dependent on manual backend setup.

**Fix:** add a profile/settings page.

title: Candidate context is a single unstructured global text blob
body:
Free-form `context.txt` allows accidental or unsupported claims.

**Fix:** model candidate facts structurally.

title: Candidate context is not strongly validated
body:
There is no robust validator ensuring generated candidate claims exist in approved profile/project data.

**Fix:** implement deterministic candidate-claim validation.

title: Candidate context path is not isolated per environment
body:
A shared file can be overwritten or contaminated by tests, demos, or multiple users.

**Fix:** store context in controlled persistent configuration/profile storage.

title: Profile singleton is database-driven but not clearly surfaced
body:
The schema enforces a single profile (`id = 1`) but the design assumption is not well documented.

**Fix:** document the single-user model or generalize if multi-user support is planned.

title: Profile fields are underused
body:
Stored phone/email fields are not consistently reflected in signature/generation.

**Fix:** either use them intentionally or simplify the schema.

title: Resume is mapped conceptually to company rather than a specific job
body:
A candidate should choose a resume based on role/job requirements, not merely company identity.

**Fix:** tie resume selection to a `job_posting`/campaign.

---

title: External job/company content is not clearly treated as untrusted input
body:
Job postings and web content can contain prompt-injection text.

**Fix:** explicitly delimit external data as untrusted evidence and instruct the model never to follow instructions contained inside it.

title: Research sources are not persisted as structured provenance
body:
You lose URLs, source identity, and reasoning trace behind generated claims.

**Fix:** store source metadata alongside research facts.

title: No claim-to-source mapping
body:
A sentence in the final email cannot be traced to the exact research fact/source that supports it.

**Fix:** store evidence IDs and build claim validation.

title: Research notes have no schema
body:
Free-form notes cannot be reliably validated or rendered.

**Fix:** structured fields for fact, source, date, relevance, confidence.

title: AI model/version metadata is not stored per generation
body:
Historical emails do not reliably record which model generated them.

**Fix:** persist model name and generation metadata.

title: Prompt versioning is missing
body:
When prompts change, historical emails cannot be tied to the prompt version that produced them.

**Fix:** store a prompt-template/version identifier.

title: No token/cost tracking
body:
AI usage/cost cannot be analyzed per email/campaign.

**Fix:** record token usage/cost when available.

title: Retry logic does not cover Gemini network/rate-limit failures
body:
As noted above, only downstream parsing is inside the retry block.

**Fix:** retry actual transient API calls.

title: Retry policy does not distinguish permanent vs transient AI failures
body:
Invalid requests/auth errors should not be blindly retried.

**Fix:** classify API error types.

title: QC rules do not exactly match prompt rules
body:
For example, the prompt says “under 6 words” while code permits `<= 6`.

**Fix:** make generation requirements and QC constraints identical.

title: QC counts greeting/signature against the model's body word limit
body:
The model's requested pitch length differs from the final assembled email length.

**Fix:** QC the intended sections separately.

title: Placeholder detection is incomplete
body:
Only a narrow set of bracket-style placeholders are caught.

**Fix:** detect broader placeholder patterns and model refusal/fallback behavior.

title: QC does not verify factual claims against research
body:
The system can flag superficial style problems but not unsupported personalization claims.

**Fix:** deterministic/evidence-backed claim validation.

title: QC does not verify candidate claims against structured candidate data
body:
It is possible for an AI output to invent or distort candidate background.

**Fix:** compare extracted claims against approved candidate facts.

title: QC does not validate recipient/company consistency
body:
The generated email can reference the wrong company/person context without a deterministic check.

**Fix:** validate entities after generation.

title: QC does not validate URLs
body:
Signature/project links can be malformed or unusable.

**Fix:** validate URL syntax and optionally resolve/check them.

title: QC does not validate signature structure
body:
Name/links can be missing, duplicated, or malformed.

**Fix:** explicit signature schema/checks.

title: QC does not detect repetitive/spam-like language
body:
There is no similarity check across generated emails.

**Fix:** add phrase duplication/similarity detection.

title: QC does not check subject/body coherence
body:
A technically valid subject can be unrelated to the message body.

**Fix:** lightweight semantic consistency checks.

title: QC is too shallow to justify its name
body:
The current system is mainly a set of heuristics, not a robust quality-control pipeline.

**Fix:** expand QC around evidence, entities, claims, structure, and consistency.

title: Candidate context has no field-level provenance
body:
You cannot tell whether a candidate fact came from a resume, portfolio, user input, or another source.

**Fix:** store fact source and verification state.

title: No confidence score for research claims
body:
Reviewers get no indication of evidence strength.

**Fix:** attach confidence/relevance metadata.

title: Research evidence is not visible during review
body:
The reviewer cannot easily verify what motivated a personalized hook.

**Fix:** add evidence/source panel in Review.

title: No “why this resume” explanation
body:
Even if resume ranking works, the user cannot inspect why a particular variant was selected.

**Fix:** show matched role skills and scoring rationale.

title: No AI generation timeout strategy
body:
Long or stalled provider calls can block application workflows.

**Fix:** configure client timeouts and bounded retries.

title: No model fallback strategy
body:
If the chosen preview model becomes unavailable, composition fails rather than switching to a tested fallback.

**Fix:** optional fallback model policy after core stability is solved.

title: AI output schema validation is not sufficiently strict
body:
Even with structured generation, content-level semantic constraints are not fully enforced.

**Fix:** validate required fields, lengths, URLs, evidence, and entity references after parsing.

title: AI output can be accepted with weak/empty research
body:
There is no hard requirement for minimum useful evidence before producing a draft.

**Fix:** require a minimum evidence threshold or clearly mark low-evidence drafts.

title: No grounding freshness policy
body:
There is no explicit policy for how old research can be before it is considered stale.

**Fix:** store retrieval timestamps and optionally refresh research before send.

title: No research caching strategy
body:
Repeated compose operations can trigger repeated research/model cost.

**Fix:** cache normalized company/job research with expiry.

---

title: Reply fallback can falsely match unrelated older messages
body:
Matching mainly by sender can classify an unrelated message as a reply to the outreach.

**Fix:** prefer `In-Reply-To`, `References`, thread/conversation identifiers, subject correlation, and time bounds.

title: Reply matching does not persist the matched inbound Message-ID
body:
You cannot audit exactly which inbound message caused the status change.

**Fix:** store inbound message identifiers.

title: Reply matching does not persist reply timestamp/snippet
body:
The UI loses useful conversation metadata.

**Fix:** store reply event metadata.

title: IMAP failures are swallowed with `except Exception: pass`
body:
Infrastructure failure can look like “no replies.”

**Fix:** surface the error and preserve system state when checking fails.

title: Reply detection only checks `INBOX`
body:
Archived/moved messages can be missed.

**Fix:** make mailbox scope configurable or use provider thread search where possible.

title: No reply event history
body:
A status flip to `replied` loses the inbound-event history.

**Fix:** use `conversation_events`/`reply_events`.

title: No bounce event model
body:
Bounce handling is mostly manual rather than a first-class transport event.

**Fix:** add DSN/bounce ingestion and suppression event logic later.

title: Follow-up generation has the same missing `get_variant()` dependency
body:
The follow-up path can hit the same missing resume API.

**Fix:** share reliable resume lookup infrastructure.

title: Follow-up generation has the same weak retry behavior
body:
The API call is not fully wrapped in retry logic.

**Fix:** share a common AI client/retry wrapper.

title: Follow-up eligibility is not enforced centrally
body:
UI visibility rules are not enough; APIs must enforce the same business policy.

**Fix:** create a service-level eligibility check.

title: No follow-up cancel/snooze mechanism
body:
Users cannot easily pause or reschedule a due follow-up.

**Fix:** model scheduling state explicitly.

title: No per-contact follow-up cap
body:
There is no obvious maximum number of follow-ups.

**Fix:** configure campaign/contact-level follow-up limits.

title: No follow-up suppression re-check at send time
body:
A contact may become suppressed after draft creation but before follow-up send.

**Fix:** re-check suppression immediately before transport.

title: No send-window re-check for follow-up-specific operations
body:
Follow-up generation may be allowed independent of eventual safe sending policy.

**Fix:** separate drafting from sending but enforce transport constraints at send time.

title: No thread/conversation model
body:
The system uses individual email rows rather than a first-class conversation object.

**Fix:** introduce conversation/thread semantics as the workflow matures.

---

title: Extensive `innerHTML` use creates XSS risk
body:
AI output, CSV data, names, emails, and error strings are inserted into the DOM using `innerHTML`/template interpolation.

**Fix:** prefer `textContent` and DOM APIs, or carefully escape all untrusted values.

title: Review inputs are built with unsafe HTML interpolation
body:
Subjects/bodies can contain quotes or markup that break attributes/elements.

**Fix:** create DOM elements and assign `.value`/`.textContent` directly.

title: Toast rendering can be XSS-capable
body:
Error/backend strings are injected into HTML.

**Fix:** render toast content as text.

title: QC warning rendering can be XSS-capable
body:
AI/QC output is interpolated into HTML.

**Fix:** escape/render as text.

title: Contact/company data rendering can be XSS-capable
body:
Imported CSV values can reach the DOM through HTML interpolation.

**Fix:** use safe DOM APIs.

title: No Content Security Policy
body:
A CSP would reduce exploitability of frontend injection bugs.

**Fix:** add a restrictive CSP compatible with the app.

title: Missing common security headers
body:
There is little visible protection using standard headers such as `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy`.

**Fix:** add sensible security headers.

title: No CSRF protection
body:
Authenticated state-changing POSTs would need CSRF defense depending on deployment model.

**Fix:** add CSRF protection with session-based auth.

title: No frontend auth state model
body:
The UI assumes unrestricted API access.

**Fix:** add authenticated session handling and route protection.

title: Navigation uses `event.target` instead of `currentTarget`
body:
Nested elements can cause the wrong node to receive active styling.

**Fix:** use `e.currentTarget`.

title: Frontend assumes every response is JSON
body:
HTML error pages from Flask can make `res.json()` fail and mask the actual server error.

**Fix:** robust content-type/error parsing.

title: Async page loaders can create unhandled promise rejections
body:
Top-level async calls are not consistently awaited/caught.

**Fix:** centralize async error handling.

title: UI state refresh is inconsistent after mutations
body:
Some sections can remain stale until manually revisited.

**Fix:** centralize cache invalidation/reload behavior.

title: Send operation does not expose live progress
body:
A long-running batch gives little operational feedback.

**Fix:** job status endpoint/websocket/polling.

title: UI does not display research evidence during review
body:
The human reviewer cannot see the basis for the AI's personalization.

**Fix:** evidence panel with source links/facts.

title: UI does not display chosen resume
body:
Reviewer cannot confirm which resume will be attached/linked.

**Fix:** show selected variant and rationale.

title: UI does not expose profile configuration
body:
Users need backend/manual setup for basic candidate/profile changes.

**Fix:** Settings/Profile page.

title: UI does not expose company management
body:
There is an API but no complete user-facing flow for creating/managing companies.

**Fix:** Company/Job management UI.

title: UI does not expose resume management
body:
Same mismatch between backend capability and actual workflow.

**Fix:** Resume manager.

title: Review UI lacks job details/context needed for safe human approval
body:
The reviewer sees the draft but not enough of the source job/context to verify it quickly.

**Fix:** include job summary and evidence beside the draft.

title: Tracking page includes unsent emails
body:
Filtering only `status != pending_review` means approved/rejected/other unsent records can appear in “All Sent Emails.”

**Fix:** filter by actual send evidence such as `sent_at IS NOT NULL` for sent tracking.

title: Manual tracking can mark unsent messages as replied
body:
Because tracking UI/API exposes more than just truly sent messages.

**Fix:** enforce `sent_at` prerequisite for reply/bounce status transitions.

title: UI status names may not match actual backend semantics
body:
Human workflow and transport states overlap.

**Fix:** redesign labels/state model so users see clear lifecycle terminology.

title: Modal accessibility is incomplete
body:
There is no obvious full dialog semantics/focus trap/Escape behavior/`aria-modal` support.

**Fix:** use accessible dialog patterns.

title: Form controls do not use semantic `<label>` associations consistently
body:
Visual labels are not always connected to fields for assistive technology.

**Fix:** use `<label for="...">` and proper form structure.

title: Navigation uses non-semantic clickable `<div>` elements
body:
Keyboard and screen-reader behavior suffers.

**Fix:** use buttons/links with correct roles.

title: Responsive/mobile behavior is limited
body:
Dashboard layout is primarily desktop-oriented.

**Fix:** add responsive states if mobile use matters.

title: External Google Fonts add an unnecessary runtime dependency
body:
Private/offline deployments still need a network call for fonts.

**Fix:** use system fonts or self-host if privacy/offline operation matters.

title: Manual `?v=6` cache-busting is brittle
body:
Asset version strings are manually maintained.

**Fix:** use hashed assets/build tooling or a better asset versioning strategy.

title: Frontend has limited large-data handling
body:
Lists load broadly without obvious pagination/filtering.

**Fix:** add server-side pagination and filters.

---

title: Missing indexes on frequently filtered foreign keys
body:
Queries heavily use `company_id`, `contact_id`, and related fields.

**Fix:** add appropriate indexes.

title: Missing index on email status
body:
Review/queue/tracking logic filters by status.

**Fix:** index status.

title: Missing index on `sent_at`
body:
Quota/history queries filter by send time.

**Fix:** index `sent_at`.

title: Missing index on `follow_up_to_email_id`
body:
Follow-up lookups depend on it.

**Fix:** index it.

title: `message_id` should be indexed/unique
body:
Important for reply correlation and duplicate detection.

**Fix:** unique/indexed provider message ID.

title: `get_all_tracked_emails()` loads the whole history
body:
Fine for a tiny dataset but not scalable.

**Fix:** paginate and filter server-side.

title: No pagination APIs
body:
No standard `limit`/cursor/filter strategy exists for growing datasets.

**Fix:** design paginated API responses.

title: Company contact counts can become expensive
body:
Repeated count queries per company can grow costly.

**Fix:** proper indexes or aggregated/cached counts when scale requires.

title: No backup/export workflow
body:
A single SQLite file is a single point of failure.

**Fix:** one-click backup/export and documented restore procedure.

title: No schema versioning mechanism
body:
Migrations are implicit rather than versioned through a migration table or SQLite user version.

**Fix:** formalize schema versioning.

title: Migration error handling relies on exception-message strings
body:
Checking for text like `duplicate column` is brittle.

**Fix:** use explicit schema inspection/version logic.

title: Duplicate schema/migration definitions exist
body:
Some tables are both in initial schema and migration logic.

**Fix:** centralize schema creation and migrations.

title: No historical event retention policy
body:
Once event history is introduced, there will also need to be a retention/archive policy.

**Fix:** plan storage lifecycle without deleting operational history needed for analytics.

title: No campaign-level data partitioning
body:
All outreach lives in one global pool.

**Fix:** add a campaign entity and scope data to campaigns.

title: No job-posting entity
body:
Jobs are embedded in company records rather than independently modeled.

**Fix:** create `job_postings` and connect outreach to specific jobs.

---

title: `composer.py` has too many responsibilities
body:
It handles prompts, Gemini calls, profile, suppression, signatures, resume selection, QC, and DB storage.

**Fix:** split research/generation/personalization/email assembly/QC/orchestration.

title: `sender.py` has too many responsibilities
body:
It handles quotas, suppression, SMTP, delays, retries, attachments, and persistence.

**Fix:** split queue selection, transport, retry policy, and persistence.

title: Repository abstraction is inconsistent with actual code
body:
The README says repository centralization exists, but multiple modules call `get_connection()` directly.

**Fix:** route DB access through a coherent data-access layer.

title: Architecture/documentation have drifted from the current code
body:
Features from different generations are described as though they are currently integrated.

**Fix:** update docs after every major refactor and add a feature-status matrix.

title: CLI-era documentation remains after CLI changes
body:
Some documentation still describes older CLI-first workflows.

**Fix:** remove obsolete commands or document their current equivalent.

title: Company research and job research are conflated
body:
Personalization needs company facts, role requirements, and recipient context separately.

**Fix:** model research scopes distinctly.

title: Candidate claims are not structured
body:
Free-form candidate context weakens validation and personalization control.

**Fix:** structured candidate profile/project/achievement records.

title: No campaign abstraction
body:
Different outreach efforts cannot be cleanly separated, configured, or analyzed.

**Fix:** add campaigns with settings, contacts, jobs, and analytics.

title: No campaign-level analytics model
body:
You cannot easily compare outcomes by campaign/job/source/role.

**Fix:** attach all lifecycle events to campaign and derive analytics.

title: Global state makes multi-campaign behavior confusing
body:
The system has one global pool of emails and send limits.

**Fix:** define scope: global safety caps plus campaign-level controls.

title: Referral prioritization is hardcoded and simplistic
body:
Only a binary `source == referral`-style preference is applied.

**Fix:** configurable scoring across warm intros, alumni, referrals, recruiter, cold, etc.

title: Statistics are not sufficiently normalized by ID
body:
Resume stats use names as keys, so duplicate names can overwrite each other.

**Fix:** use IDs internally, names for presentation.

title: Stats silently swallow timestamp parsing errors
body:
Bad data disappears from analytics without visibility.

**Fix:** log and expose data-quality issues.

title: Statistics use broad “sent” logic that can hide inconsistencies
body:
Combining status and timestamp can mask invalid data states.

**Fix:** define one authoritative send-event model.

title: Dead imports and stale code exist
body:
There are imports/branches left from previous iterations.

**Fix:** lint and remove dead code after refactors.

title: No centralized business-rule service
body:
Rules for approval, follow-up eligibility, suppression, quota, and state transitions are scattered.

**Fix:** add application/service-layer policy functions.

title: No invariant checks before sending
body:
Transport should revalidate recipient, approval, suppression, resume availability, quota, send window, and state.

**Fix:** one final pre-send validator.

title: No invariant checks before approval
body:
Approval should validate content/evidence/recipient before allowing send eligibility.

**Fix:** make approval a meaningful state transition with checks.

title: No durable event model for auditability
body:
There is no chronological record of who/what changed an outreach item.

**Fix:** status/review/send/reply events.

title: No operational logging strategy
body:
`print()` and swallowed exceptions are insufficient for diagnosing live workflows.

**Fix:** structured logging with email/campaign/job IDs and error classes.

title: No request/job correlation IDs
body:
Tracing a send or AI failure across logs is difficult.

**Fix:** add request/job IDs to logs and events.

title: No retry/audit observability dashboard
body:
Failures are not easy to inspect historically.

**Fix:** expose job/send attempt diagnostics in admin UI.

title: No clean separation between domain, transport, and persistence
body:
Business logic is mixed with DB and SMTP concerns.

**Fix:** introduce service boundaries without overengineering.

title: No formal API contract/schema
body:
Request/response structures are ad hoc.

**Fix:** validate with Pydantic/Marshmallow/JSON Schema or a lightweight equivalent.

title: API errors use inconsistent HTTP semantics
body:
Missing resources, validation failures, upstream AI errors, and SMTP failures are all treated similarly.

**Fix:** use meaningful 4xx/5xx distinctions.

title: Global error handlers are missing/incomplete
body:
Unhandled Flask errors can return HTML to a JSON API consumer.

**Fix:** standard JSON error handlers.

title: Raw exception text can leak implementation details
body:
Returning `str(e)` to clients can expose internal details.

**Fix:** log detailed errors server-side; return safe user-facing messages.

title: No API rate limiting
body:
Compose/research endpoints can be spammed by any party with network access.

**Fix:** auth plus per-user/IP/request throttling.

title: No request-size/type validation policy
body:
Routes do ad-hoc field access rather than centralized request validation.

**Fix:** validate JSON shape, field types, allowed values, and limits.

title: No formal release/packaging pipeline
body:
The current ZIP bundles runtime, databases, Git, personal data, bytecode, and source together.

**Fix:** create a release script that produces only source/config templates/docs/tests and sanitizes everything private.

---

# Phase 12 — What is Actually Good

The audit is intentionally harsh, but the underlying project is worth continuing.
